en: One Night in an Onsen Ryokan: Bathing, Dinner, and Quiet
zh: 温泉与旅馆的一夜：洗浴、晚餐、安静
ja: 温泉と旅館の一夜：入浴、夕食、静けさ

p.src: Before leaving Lake Ashi, the old road, or a museum, open the ryokan confirmation. With a dinner-inclusive stay, meal service may depend on arriving by a stated deadline, and station pickup may require a reservation. The four guides stop sightseeing before dark and reach the mountain ryokan with only their small bags. At check-in they confirm the dinner place and service window, public-bath and cleaning hours, any private-bath booking, breakfast, checkout, and next-morning pickup. If a bus or ropeway delay threatens arrival, contact the property before deciding what to drop. The easiest thing to remove is the pre-dinner soak, not the dinner already booked with the room.

caption.zh: 把旅馆确认邮件当成当天最后一段交通的终点。按约定时段抵达，登记时一次确认晚餐、浴场、早餐、退房与次日接送。
caption.ja: 宿の予約確認を、その日の移動の終点として使う。指定時刻までに着き、夕食、浴場、朝食、チェックアウト、翌朝の送迎を一度に確かめる。
caption.en: Treat the ryokan confirmation as the endpoint of the day's transport. Arrive within the stated window, then confirm dinner, baths, breakfast, checkout, and next-morning pickup together.

p.src: The sequence diagram uses no universal clock because the real times are in the booking. The normal line is: arrive before the property's deadline; check in and confirm dinner and bath access; bathe first only if the schedule has room; attend dinner; return quietly to the room; consider a morning bath only while it is open; then take breakfast, check out, and make the next connection. The late-arrival branch is shorter: call the property, confirm what can still be served, check in, protect dinner, and move bathing to later or to the morning. Follow on-site guidance for the shoe boundary, keys, dining room, and yukata. Save this sequence rather than assuming every ryokan follows the same timetable.

caption.zh: 一夜没有统一时刻表：先保住约定的抵达与晚餐，再把泡汤放进剩余时间。若晚点，先联系旅馆。
caption.ja: 一泊の共通時刻表はない。到着と夕食の予約を優先し、残った時間に入浴を置く。遅れるときは先に宿へ連絡する。
caption.en: There is no universal overnight timetable. Protect the agreed arrival and dinner first, then place the bath in the remaining time; call the ryokan when delayed.

p.src: Hakone's Edo-period Seven Springs were Yumoto, Tonosawa, Dogashima, Miyanoshita, Sokokura, Kiga, and Ashinoyu. Longer therapeutic stays existed alongside the one-night form of toji that suited travel on the Tokaido. Later development widened the resort into the historical frame now called the Seventeen Springs. That number helps explain the growth of the onsen landscape; it is not a water menu for individual properties. Hakone Town also records that hot-water supply to areas without their own springs began in 1965 and later extended towards Moto-Hakone and Hakone. When booking, check what feeds the specific room and bath and how the property labels it. The district name alone is not enough.

p.src: After check-in, put down the luggage and prepare in the room rather than heading straight to the bath. Wearing the property's yukata, the four guides pause in the dry common corridor before separating at the posted entrances. They read the access notice, leave phones, cameras, and valuables in the room safe or the locker specified by the property, and carry only the towels and keys required there. If a private bath has a reserved slot, confirm its start and finish. If dinner is near, do not force a hurried soak. Shared baths follow the facility's access arrangement, and companions need not choose the same bathing option. Privacy, health, steps, and handrails are conditions to check before passing the threshold.

caption.zh: 浴场入口是从客房习惯切换到共同空间的门槛。手机留在干区，先看开放和清扫时间，再按洗净身体、入池的顺序行动。
caption.ja: 浴場入口は、客室から共有空間へ切り替わる境目。携帯電話は乾いた場所に置き、利用・清掃時間を確かめてから、体を洗って湯船へ入る。
caption.en: The bath entrance marks the shift from guest room to shared space. Leave the phone in the dry area, check operating and cleaning hours, wash first, and only then enter the bath.

p.src: The shared-bath sequence is straightforward. Undress in the changing room; unless the facility explicitly permits it, do not enter in swimwear. Sit at a washing station, wash, and rinse away all soap before using kakeyu to acclimatize to the water. Tie up long hair and keep the small towel out of the bath. Leave the phone outside and take no photographs. In the water, do not swim or splash, and keep conversation low. If the bath feels too hot or you become dizzy or unwell, get out rather than trying to complete a set time. Do not schedule a very hot or prolonged soak around drinking alcohol. Dry off before returning to the changing area, and follow any posted instructions about rinsing and hygiene.

p.src: Ask six questions before booking. May a guest with tattoos use the public bath? Is the private bath in the room or booked for a separate time? Does that particular bath use natural onsen water? What are its opening and cleaning periods? Are there steps, handrails, a shower, and a bathing stool between changing room and pool? What washing option remains if the public bath is unsuitable? Hakone properties currently publish both accepting and restrictive tattoo policies, so do not assume one rule applies across the destination. If privacy or tattoo access determines whether you can bathe, obtain the property's answer in writing before payment. Private does not mean step-free, and an in-room tub is not automatically onsen; verify water source, time, access, and personal mobility separately.

p.src: Ryokan dinner is not restaurant service available at any hour; it is an appointment attached to the room plan. The four guides sit at the confirmed time while seasonal small dishes, soup, a grilled course, and rice arrive in sequence. The scene shows the pace of a multi-course meal without passing a general kaiseki form off as a food unique to Hakone. Some properties serve in the room, some use a dining room, and some sell plans without dinner. Raise ingredients and drinks you cannot consume before the kitchen finishes the dishes. A sequence of courses takes time and should be followed by rest. If drinking alcohol, do not make a hot soak a compulsory after-dinner event. Leave time to rest after dinner instead of packing bathing, dinner, and another excursion into the same evening.

caption.zh: 一泊二食的晚餐是预约，不是随时开放的餐厅。按开始时段入席；过敏和饮食限制要在订房前写清楚并取得答复。
caption.ja: 一泊二食の夕食は予約の一部で、いつでも入れる食堂ではない。開始時刻に席へ着き、アレルギーや食事制限は予約前に書面で伝えて回答を得る。
caption.en: Dinner in a two-meal stay is an appointment, not an all-hours restaurant. Sit down at the agreed time, and disclose allergies or dietary restrictions in writing before booking.

p.src: Confirm whether the plan includes dinner, where it is served, and the latest arrival time. Send dietary restrictions by the property's deadline; the kitchen may not be able to replace stock, sauce, or prepared dishes that day. For a serious allergy, ask in writing whether the ingredient and cross-contact can be avoided. If the property cannot give that assurance, choose another plan. A short Chinese-Japanese-English ingredient card supports on-site confirmation but does not replace an advance answer. If transport is delayed, contact the ryokan before dinner begins.

p.src: Tatami and futon are common, but they are not identical across every ryokan or room type. Some properties lay out bedding during dinner; others offer permanent beds or mixed Japanese-Western rooms. Chairs, table height, in-room shower, toilet, stairs, and lift access also vary. A listing that says “Japanese room” is not enough: inspect the exact room type and ask about steps from entrance to room, then from room to toilet and bath. Mention knee or leg difficulty, trouble rising from the floor, frequent nighttime movement, or the need to wash in the room before payment. Choosing a bed, chair, or private shower does not make a ryokan stay less authentic. A room that lets you sleep well leaves enough energy for Hakone the next day.

p.src: Before sleep, write one line: bath and cleaning hours, breakfast, checkout and payment, luggage, pickup or next departure. Take a morning bath only when it is open and you feel well; skip it when cleaning or breakfast conflicts. Leave a margin between breakfast and a connection that cannot be missed. Before leaving, check the safe, charging points, cupboards, and yukata sleeves, then return borrowed items. For luggage storage or forwarding, verify the cutoff and destination. Depart for the service you checked instead of squeezing in one more soak. The next chapter fits black eggs, amazake, and full meals into the daytime route.
